note: Triggering + output-quality eval. Run on claude.ai without subagents: load the skill the description should select, follow it, then grade the output against assertions. Assertions are written so a wrong-skill answer fails them.

evals.name: missing-edges-under-load
evals.prompt: my dependency map is missing edges under load
evals.expected_output: Diagnose the incremental materialized view self-join as the likely cause, explain the insert-block semantics, prescribe the assembler + refreshable reconciler fix, and give a way to confirm before changing anything.

assertions.text: Names the classic materialized view self-join on spans as the prime suspect
Explains that an MV SELECT sees only the current insert block, not the table
Explains WHY parent and child land in different batches (parent finishes after child; collector flushes on size/time)
Prescribes moving stitching into the stateful assembler and keeping MVs single-table
Mentions the refreshable MV reconciler and the >2% divergence alert
Offers a concrete confirmation query or check before changing code
Does not blame sampling or the collector as the primary cause

evals.name: detector-alerts-too-much
evals.prompt: the detector alerts too much, tune it
evals.expected_output: Refuse to tune blind: run the eval set first, read precision and the null-case outcome, then change one knob and re-measure. Name the specific gates and the boiling-frog risk of raising alpha.

assertions.text: Insists on measuring with the eval set before changing thresholds
Points at the null case as the false-positive measurement
Names specific knobs: min_requests, sustained_cycles, threshold_ms, alpha
Warns that raising alpha risks the boiling-frog failure / baseline chasing noise
Reminds that the baseline must only update on healthy observations
Changes one variable at a time and re-runs the eval
Considers that the alerts may be correct (real regression) before assuming the detector is wrong

evals.name: downsize-to-4gb-vps
evals.prompt: I want to move TraceMap to a 4GB VPS to save money, will it fit?
evals.expected_output: Say no with the measured component floor table (~7GB), then give real options: Oracle free tier, CX32, or a genuinely trimmed profile with named tradeoffs.

assertions.text: Answers no, it will not fit, without hedging
Cites the ~7GB measured component floor
Breaks down RAM by component rather than asserting a single number
Offers Oracle Always-Free and Hetzner CX32 as the real options
If a trimmed profile is offered, names what is lost
Does not silently accept the 4GB premise
